# Glossary {#sec-glossary}

Short definitions of the terms used throughout the manual. Fuller treatment is
in @sec-concepts.

**Allele** — one observed DNA sequence at a locus. Two isolates share an allele
when their sequence there is identical.

**Allele profile** — an isolate's set of allele calls, one per locus; the row that
represents it in the isolate × locus table.

**Allelic distance** — the number of loci at which two profiles carry different
alleles; the Hamming distance between profiles (@sec-concepts-distance).

**AMR determinant** — a gene or mutation known to contribute to antimicrobial
resistance. A genotype, not a measured phenotype (@sec-concepts-amr).

**Analysis** — a named container of saved plots, stored inside the database file
(@sec-dashboard).

**Assembly** — the reconstructed genome of one isolate, as a FASTA file
(`.fasta`, `.fa` or `.fna`); the input to typing.

**cgMLST (core-genome MLST)** — typing an isolate by its allele at every locus in
a standardized core-genome scheme (@sec-concepts).

**Classical MLST** — typing ~7 housekeeping genes to assign a sequence type
[@maiden1998mlst].

**Cluster threshold** — the allelic distance within which isolates are grouped
into one cluster on an MST; set under **Options > Clustering**, and defaulting to
the value published with your scheme (@sec-mst-cluster).

**Collapse threshold** — the allelic distance at or below which an MST merges the
nodes a branch joins, set under **Options > Collapsing**. Zero by default, which
merges only identical profiles (@sec-mst-collapse).

**Completeness** — the share of a scheme's loci that received a confident allele
call for an isolate; the first quality check on a typing run
(@sec-typing-results).

**Core genome** — the set of loci present in essentially all members of a species.

**Content fingerprint (hash)** — a value derived from data's own bytes, used to
recognise the same allele or the same assembly across databases
(@sec-concepts-hashing).

**Custom variable** — a field you define yourself, typed and stored inside the
database alongside the standard metadata (@sec-browser-custom).

**Epidemic curve** — cases plotted against date of collection (@sec-concepts-epi).

**Generate** — the button at the top of a plot's left sidebar that recomputes the
data behind it. Needed only for the isolate selection, the **Missing values**
policy, a Tree's **Algorithm**, and the Map's geocoding pass (@sec-viz-generate).

**Hamming distance** — the count of positions at which two equal-length vectors
differ [@hamming1950].

**Isolate** — one sampled bacterial strain; the unit of analysis.

**Locus** — a defined position (gene) in the genome that a scheme types.

**Minimum spanning tree (MST)** — the lowest-total-length set of links connecting
all isolates, with each isolate a visible node (@sec-concepts-mst)
[@prim1957; @kruskal1956].

**Missing call (NA)** — a locus with no confident allele call; handled by one of
three policies (ignore / category / omit) chosen under **Options > Missing
values** when computing distance (@sec-concepts-distance).

**Plot tab** — one independent figure in the Visualization workspace, with its
own isolate selection, controls and save target. Its type is fixed at creation
(@sec-viz-tabs).

**Neighbour-Joining (NJ)** — a tree method that does not assume a constant rate of
change; branch lengths vary freely [@saitou1987nj].

**Novel allele** — a sequence at a locus that the scheme has not recorded before;
it is stored and given a new identifier during typing (@sec-typing).

**Provenance** — the record of how an isolate was typed: assembly, scheme,
thresholds and tool versions (@sec-typing-provenance).

**Scheme** — the species-specific definition of loci, allele nomenclature and
reference genome that typing runs against (@sec-schemes).

**Sequence type (ST)** — a registered name for a (classical-MLST) allele profile.

**Staging** — holding a partner's imported *profiles* (identifiers, not
sequences) for distance-only comparison (@sec-interop-staging).

**UPGMA** — a tree method assuming a constant rate of change, producing an
ultrametric (level-tipped) tree [@sokal1958upgma].

**Virulence / stress element** — a gene contributing to pathogenicity, or to
tolerance of biocides/metals/stress, reported by the AMR screen alongside AMR
genes (@sec-amr).
